author: nick-choudhary
description: MCP server that gives AI assistants access to LinkedIn Sales Navigator contact and account search by driving a real, logged-in browser on your machine and capturing Sales Navigator's own search API responses.
name: LinkedIn Sales Navigator MCP

prompts.name: sales_nav_search_workflow
prompts.description: Playbook for a prospecting run with this server: verify the session, run a Sales Navigator search URL, then sample or export the saved records.

resources.name: saved_queries
resources.description: Every saved Sales Navigator search and its progress (url_hash, url, scraper_type, status, last_page, total_available, records_count). Attach this to see what is already in the local store before deciding to search again.

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Search people/leads by driving Sales Navigator in the logged-in browser and capturing its search API responses. Results are saved to the local database automatically; this tool returns a small summary, not the records (call export_results or get_results for the data). Build the search in Sales Navigator (title / geography / industry / seniority / keyword filters), copy the URL from the address bar, and pass it here. Saved lead lists work too. Resumable: the search URL is hashed to a query id; calling again with the same URL resumes from the next page instead of restarting.

pages.description: How many 25-result pages to fetch in THIS call (1-10). Call again to continue past that.

resume.description: If true (default), continue from where a prior run of this same URL stopped. If false, start from page 1 (records already saved are kept and de-duplicated).

refresh.description: If true, forget this query's saved progress and records and re-scrape from page 1.

include_raw.description: Keep LinkedIn's raw element JSON alongside each record (useful when a field looks wrong).

tools.name: search_accounts
tools.description: Search companies/accounts by driving Sales Navigator in the logged-in browser and capturing its search API responses. Results are saved to the local database automatically; this tool returns a small summary, not the records (call export_results or get_results for the data). Build the search in Sales Navigator (industry / headcount / geography / growth filters), copy the URL from the address bar, and pass it here. Saved account lists work too. Resumable: the search URL is hashed to a query id; calling again with the same URL resumes from the next page instead of restarting.

pages.description: How many 25-result pages to fetch in THIS call (1-10).

resume.description: If true (default), continue from where a prior run of this same URL stopped. If false, start from page 1 (saved records are kept and de-duplicated).

refresh.description: If true, forget this query's saved progress and records and re-scrape from page 1.

include_raw.description: Keep LinkedIn's raw element JSON alongside each record.

tools.name: list_queries
tools.description: List every saved search and its progress. For each: url_hash, url, scraper_type, status (new|in_progress|paused|complete), last_page, total_available, records_count. Use a url_hash with export_results or get_results.

tools.name: export_results
tools.description: Export a saved query's records to files under the output folder.

url_or_hash.description: The query's url_hash (from list_queries) or its original search URL.

format.description: 'json', 'csv', or 'both' (default). JSON is the full store view; CSV is flat columns for spreadsheets.

include_raw.description: Include LinkedIn's raw element JSON in the export.

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Pull a bounded slice of a saved query's records into the conversation for analysis. Bounded on purpose; for large sets, prefer export_results and analyze the file with code rather than loading everything into context.

url_or_hash.description: The query's url_hash or original search URL.

offset.description: Records to skip (for paging through the sample).

tools.name: check_session_status
tools.description: Check whether the browser profile has a live Sales Navigator session. Launches (or reuses) the browser and verifies it lands on a signed-in /sales page. Use this first when searches fail; it tells you if you need to run --login again. Returns logged_in (bool), plus the profile directory and headless setting for this server.
